scenario.title: KHALKHIN GOL - 3 JUL 1939
intro.text:
KHALKHIN GOL - 3 JUL 1939

Khalkhin Gol River, Mongolian People's Republic

The Japanese crossed the Khalkhin Gol river in the north, occupied the Baintsagan hills and tried to surround our troops with a two-pronged assault. Carry out a vigorous counterattack, thwart the enemy intentions and occupy the Japanese positions west and east of the river!

ORDERS
Capture all VH!

CORE (recommended)
2x Tank
3x Infantry (+1)
1x Reconnaissance
1x Artillery
1x Fighter Aircraft (+1)
header.act: ACT I — LESSONS BEFORE THE GREAT WAR
header.location: Khalkhin Gol, Mongolian People's Republic — 3 July 1939
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.reaction-briliant.text: Both Khasan heights were retaken before the Japanese staff could reinforce the saddle. The speed impressed Moscow; the roads required to hold them did not appear in the communiqué.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.reaction-victory.text: The border posts stand again at Khasan. So do the recovery tractors, because holding a height and reaching it remain separate problems.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.reaction-tactical.text: Khasan ended with our flag on the heights and too many battalions below them. The official map is tidy. The transport returns are not.
line.callback-choice-a.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.callback-choice-a.text: At Khasan you kept the assault moving until both heights were under pressure. The report praised resolve and buried the transport losses in an appendix. I did not.
line.callback-choice-b.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.callback-choice-b.text: The engineers owned the timetable at Khasan and brought the guns through the mud. On this steppe their lanes are hundreds of kilometres long, but the principle has supporters now.
line.earned-decision.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.earned-decision.text: Both Khasan heights were still in our hands when the front stabilised. The engineer companies that kept their roads open are available for one new assignment.
line.earned-decision.choice.attach-khasa: Keep the Khasan engineers together as a field detachment.
Add an experienced eight-strength 1936 engineer detachment to the core.
line.earned-decision.choice.spread-khasa: Return the companies to their formations and circulate their methods.
Give every infantry and artillery formation 12 experience instead of receiving another unit.
line.earned-a-response.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.earned-a-response.text: They keep their tractors, bridging stores, and company organisation. Give them a road and they will tell us whether the map has lied about it.
line.earned-b-response.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.earned-b-response.text: No new box appears on the strength return. The value is that every division now plans its road before it announces its arrival time.
line.scene-0.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.scene-0.text: A windstorm lifts the steppe into the command tent. On the map the river is a blue pencil stroke; outside, fuel trucks, Mongolian cavalry, tank columns, and field kitchens are all trying to use the same tracks.
line.scene-1.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.scene-1.text: After Khasan, Moscow asked why courage had arrived before shells and ambulances. If we go deep here, the answer had better travel in the same column as the tanks.
line.decision.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.decision.text: A local counterattack can throw them off Baintsagan. A deeper blow can also cut the crossing and trap the force west of the river—but only if our columns keep moving after the first contact.
Drive beyond the heights and cut the bridgehead from its crossings.
Give tank and reconnaissance formations 20 experience each and fully refuel the core, but do not replace losses or ammunition.
line.decision.choice.secure-the-river.te: Crush the bridgehead methodically and rebuild the river position before pursuing.
line.decision.choice.secure-the-river.hi: Restore every core formation to at least nine strength with full fuel and ammunition, and give artillery 15 experience.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.choice-a-0.text: The heights are not the finish line. Mobile detachments will pass through as soon as the first position breaks and aim for the crossings.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.choice-a-1.text: Cut the crossings, but write the fuel limit beside the arrow. I will stop the exploitation myself if the tankers begin reporting hope instead of kilometres.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.choice-b-0.text: The river line comes first. Every captured height receives guns and supply before the next one is attacked.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.choice-b-1.text: You are making success halt at the river. Give me a release condition now, or every cautious headquarters will discover one more height that must be secured first.
line.post-0.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.post-0.text: Fuel limits, crossing times, and the release condition go on one sheet. If Antonov loses it in the dust, he stops.
